newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rig count down 20 to 825 in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rig count down 20 to 825 in latest week.

text.p: The number of rigs exploring for oil and natural gas in the United States stood at 825 as of Friday, down 20 from the prior week and 121 above the year-ago total of 704, Baker Hughes Inc. reported Friday.
The number of rigs drilling on land fell by 15 to 689, while rigs working offshore fell six to 111. The number of rigs active in inland waters was up one to 25.
Among the individual states, the biggest changes occurred in Texas, which was down six, New Mexico and Oklahoma, which were down five and Wyoming, which was down four.

A total of 346 rigs were exploring for crude oil, down 17 from last week. The number of rigs searching for gas was down three at 477, while the number of miscellaneous drilling projects remained at two.
There were 173 rigs drilling directionally, 60 drilling horizontally and 592 drilling vertically.
In Canada, the number of working rigs surged by 52 in the week to 410 vs. 352 a year ago.
The weekly rig count reflects the number of rigs exploring for oil and gas, not those producing oil and gas.
Separately, there were 160 rigs under contract in the U.S. Gulf as of Jan. 10, up one from the period ending Jan. 3, Offshore Data Services said.
The utilization rate for rigs working in the Gulf, based on a total fleet of 181, was 88.4 percent.
The number of working rigs in the European/Mediterranean area remained the same this week at 106 rigs under contract out of a total fleet of 107, a utilization rate of 99.1 pct.
The worldwide rig count rose one to 557 out of a total fleet of 606, making the utilization rate 91.9 percent.
